objective: Port the complete Pi AI package into the Go ai module, preserving upstream contracts and observable behavior. The original TypeScript is a test oracle, not the Go implementation.
reference_note: Reference source lives outside this module. Go tests use checked-in expected data, never TypeScript implementation code. The full provider migration is still in progress.
integration_status: Native Go implementation only; no Pi subprocess, Bun/Node runtime, or third_party source dependency. Existing provider adapters are being migrated to the ported contracts.
next: Native Completions, Responses and Anthropic Messages include streamSimple and host routing. Anthropic workload federation is admitted by ModelTier for scoped/process configuration when no API key or explicit refresh callback is supplied. The concrete Anthropic messaging-client injection boundary is ported. Continue alternate-provider adapters, user OAuth lifecycle and remaining provider APIs. Audit SDK/Unicode/numeric edges before switching the app default and retiring the bridge.
Complete Pi model/options/provider contracts, model collections, auth and catalog support.
Port all API implementations and route Go callers through them.
Port remaining images/classifiers, OAuth, transport/session, utilities and CLI/build equivalents where applicable.
Run provider-level differential request/event/error fixtures and audit every source module against current upstream.

Before marking the port complete, remove TypeScript reference sources and fixture generators, the development worker/bridge, and port-only Bun dependencies/configuration. Retain Go code/tests, verified JSON fixtures and provenance/license notices; verify builds and tests without the removed tooling.

modules.remaining: Native Codex request construction is ported: instructions, transcript/tool conversion, strict/grammar contracts, mid-conversation tool declarations, cache identity, nullable controls and reasoning maps. The builder consumes an already selected cacheSessionID; transport-level cache selection/clamping remains outside it, as in Pi. It does not spread generic sampling parameters into Codex requests. Codex event mapping and shared Responses accumulation are ported, including first-terminal admission, end_turn, error precedence, status normalization, signatures, tool scratch cleanup and Codex service-tier pricing. The Codex SSE parser preserves LF framing, residual EOF, skipped DONE markers and streaming UTF-8. Codex URL resolution, JWT account extraction and SSE/WebSocket header precedence are ported, including atob Latin-1 decoding and nullable overrides. Platform user-agent text is checked separately from the portable fixtures. Exact malformed-header/JSON diagnostics and malformed typed events remain unproven. Retry classification, numeric/HTTP-date Retry-After delays, delay ceilings and quota error formatting are ported with source fixtures. Nonstandard JavaScript Date.parse formats remain unproven. StreamCodexResponsesSSE now executes explicit SSE in Go with zstd level-3 compression, per-request credentials, cache-key clamping, payload/response/event callbacks, HTTP retries and header-only timeout. Differential HTTP fixtures compare headers, decompressed request JSON, callback order and final messages; exact compressed bytes are not established. Real local HTTP tests cover header timeout, longer response-body lifetime and cancellation. StreamCodexResponsesSimpleSSE ports simple-mode option filtering, thinking-level clamping/mapping and synchronous explicit-key admission through the Go SSE transport. WebSocket continuation request selection is ported: settings and previous input/output prefix must retain JSON.stringify identity, including key order; mismatches invalidate continuation and preserve the full request. Socket cache ownership, reuse, busy-session isolation, idle/age expiry and explicit closure are ported with source fixtures and concurrent ownership checks. The WebSocket event queue/parser handles terminal admission, binary UTF-8/BOM, close/error metadata, cancellation and idle timeout with source fixtures. Exact malformed-JSON diagnostic text remains unproven. A native Gorilla WebSocket connection now drives the parser with one lifetime reader, per-request listener attachment/detachment, serialized sends, handshake timeout/cancellation and cache-compatible readiness. Local real-socket tests verify two requests on one cached socket, binary frames, early close metadata, idle timeout, cancellation and blocked HTTP-upgrade cleanup. Internal WebSocket request orchestration now acquires/releases leases, sends response.create, starts output on the first mapped event, retains typed callback failures, rejects unfinished tool calls before caching and persists continuation from converted assistant output. 110 source cases compare request JSON, event snapshots, output, error class, close behavior, continuation and debug statistics; a real socket test verifies full context then a delta request with previous_response_id. Internal transport policy now composes with WebSocket requests: one independent retry each for connection-limit and missing-continuation errors, start deduplication, non-transport error exclusion, no mid-message fallback and sticky per-session SSE fallback with reset. Original-stream fixtures verify 19 decision sequences, including explicit WebSocket fallback, after-start retry and cross-request failure memory. StreamCodexResponses and StreamCodexResponsesSimple now provide public combined native transport selection using shared immutable request preparation. SSE fallback reuses payload/auth/headers without invoking onPayload again; SSE source fixtures now execute through the combined entry points. Local end-to-end tests verify WebSocket reuse, fallback, sticky session bypass, explicit SSE and callback counts. CloseCodexResponsesSessions releases cached sockets without resetting fallback, matching source cleanup semantics. Transport diagnostics carry type, timestamp, error name/message/code and fallback/start/request-byte details; JavaScript stack serialization is not reproduced. Debug request/connection/context/failure/fallback counters and optional last-value fields are ported with source fixtures. GetCodexWebSocketDebugStats returns detached snapshots; ResetCodexWebSocketDebugStats atomically resets counters and fallback memory without closing sockets, while socket cleanup preserves them. Concurrent counter and reset/close ownership tests pass. Malformed URL/JSON diagnostics and timer overflow edges remain pending. NativeProviderStream now dispatches the Codex API through StreamCodexResponsesSimple. NativeAgent tracks nonempty Codex session IDs actually used and closes their cached sockets after its requests settle. Real host tests prove per-request getApiKey refresh, account-isolated sockets, missing-key rejection and close cleanup without erasing counters. Codex HTTP failures now preserve status and cloned retry headers outside Pi message JSON. An internal failure observer supplies the original cause before publishing an error result; the pool bridge translates only typed HTTP failures to the existing host ProviderError, preserving 401/403 rotation, 429 retry hints and the 403 concurrency exception without guessing from error text. StreamCodexResponsesPooled now acquires a per-attempt credential, runs the native simple stream, reports the same account, and rotates only typed authentication failures before visible text/thinking/tool events. It retains the existing 64-attempt and repeated-credential guards, avoids reporting transient concurrency caps, buffers replay-safe metadata and shares a payload mutex so forwarded live partial/result pointers remain identical. Tests cover rotation, repeated tokens, quota, concurrency, callback errors, success and progressive identity. This is a host adapter rather than an upstream Pi pool feature. The native runner now selects a bound Codex pool stream when the resolved tier supplies a TokenSource. Its model binding preserves endpoint/model checks and returns null from getApiKey without acquiring or serializing credentials; Acquire/Report stays inside the native stream. The full runner test proves auth rotation, final answer, exact account reporting and no credentials in native state/telemetry. Public BindPi/worker paths, custom stream overrides and other OAuth vendors retain explicit rejection until separately integrated. Fallback rung resolution is now shared with legacy construction and native binding, preserving provider-row identity, source/key ownership, API dialect and existing window rules without acquiring tokens. Native binding returns callbacks and dispatcher together. Built-in native runner ladders now perform scoped preparation, retries/escalation, row-aware refresh, durable selection before effects and recovery of the retained model. Children and auxiliary summaries own independent ladders. Real HTTP runner tests cover compaction, tools, fork, resume and selection-write failure; explicit custom streams and workers still reject configured fallback. The legacy pooled CodexProvider remains for legacy callers.

Existing loop fixtures cover optional nulls and common schema failures. ParseJSNumber is also shared by the native Anthropic federation expiry path. Another 113 cases cover 16 built-in format assertions, coercion, unknown formats, sibling diagnostic ordering, union checks and reference checks; patterns are translated from locked TypeBox 1.3.27. Another 190 hostname/IDN cases cover raw punycode, encoded-label and domain length limits, normalization, contextual joiners, bidi rules, malformed ACE labels, raw-decoder UTF-16 pair joining and corresponding Unicode/ACE inputs. Another 258 URL/IRI/reference cases cover relative references, Unicode hosts, IPv4/IPv6, ports, file/custom schemes, whitespace, percent encoding and the IPvFuture UTF-16 length boundary; runtime validation uses a pinned pure-Go WHATWG parser. Another 145 regex-format cases cover Unicode syntax admission, legacy and .NET extension rejection, named/numeric capture references, disjoint duplicate capture names, scoped modifiers, assertion quantifiers and class range endpoints. The pinned oracle accepts non-ASCII identity escapes; that behavior is retained. Another 42 matching cases cover named/numeric capture ordering, nested captures, forward/optional references, repeated duplicate alternatives and Unicode/escaped names; lowering preserves original pattern diagnostics. Another 101 tool-path cases cover Unicode property syntax, aliases, binary properties, general categories, scripts, script extensions, complements and mixed classes. TestPiUnicodePropertyOracle checks 419 generated property sets with 86903 boundary/interior probes in four matching forms and compiles all 1627 accepted aliases. The generator pins Bun 1.3.14 / Unicode 15.1 and enumerates all 1114112 code points; native runtime uses only Go tables. Another 205 cases cover scoped dot-all and multiline matching with all four JavaScript line terminators, modifier inheritance/disable/restore, CRLF, lookarounds, named captures and literal metacharacters. Parser-aware dot/anchor lowering replaces the unconditional dot rewrite. Another 145 tool cases cover repeated capture resets, optional descendants, duplicate names, bounded/lazy repetition, backtracking, lookarounds and optional/mandatory empty iterations. TestPiRegexpRepetitionOracle adds 11648 comparisons across all 364 a/b/c strings through length five and 32 source patterns. Lowering uses backtrackable capture resets and nullable-iteration guards, including right-to-left lookbehind. Progress flags replace repeated suffix/prefix scans and distinguish consuming atoms/nonempty references from lookaround-only activity. BenchmarkPiNullableRepetition on Apple M1 Pro (3 measured iterations) reduced the 8192-character case from 160.8 ms to 2.4 ms per match; this is a focused benchmark, not a general regex performance bound. Another 277 tool cases cover pinned Unicode admission in hostname/ACE/IDN-email formats, capture identifiers and escaped name delimiters. Hostname category/script checks and Unicode format patterns share the generated property tables. The native capture grammar rejects Letter_Number and Other_ID_Start/Other_ID_Continue exceptions as observed in the pinned JavaScriptCore runtime. TestPiUnicodePropertyOracle adds 4640 capture-name probes, each in literal/escaped start/continuation forms, and checks direct property lookups against all 86903 property probes. Escaped greater-than characters terminate names and references while preserving the following pattern body. TestPiLoopOracle also checks literal tool-name diagnostics against Pi, including quotes, backslashes, controls and Unicode; validation errors no longer apply Go string quoting. Thirteen tool cases and TestPiRegexpCharactersOracle verify word escapes/boundaries, class unions/complements, scoped ignore-case, lookbehind and repetition: 71 patterns over 255 inputs, 17340 matching comparisons for valid patterns, and 2224128 comparisons covering both word sets over every representable Unicode scalar. Explicit word sets and lookarounds replace the backend Unicode boundary behavior; scoped exact word branches avoid dotted-I/long-s folding differences.
